items.slide_topic: Counterpoint: faster releases are not necessarily faster progress
items.headline: Why AI model releases feel nonstop
items.dek: OpenAI and Anthropic are putting out more models, but much of the acceleration comes from repackaging existing advances for new price points.
items.outlet: Fast Company (read via Yahoo Finance syndication)
items.author: Mark Sullivan
items.caption: Pre-dates the chart by 6 days and does not cite it, but gives the cleanest counterpoint with numbers.
items.notes: Syndicated copy loaded: https://finance.yahoo.com/technology/ai/articles/why-ai-model-releases-feel-102100600.html. fastcompany.com itself shows a 'Verification Required' captcha to the headless browser and the Yahoo copy renders ads/video placeholder, so NO screenshot was kept. Verbatim: 'It feels like new model releases are accelerating, and they are, but many of the new releases are models that repackage (and often reprice) the capabilities of earlier flagship models.' and 'Anthropic's release cadence for frontier models has roughly doubled during 2026, from a model every 46 days in the first half to every 26 days so far in the second; OpenAI's release cadence has increased from every 46 days in the first half of the year to every 51 days so far in the second. But the time between genuinely new flagship frontier models hasn't changed much during 2026 for either company, the release dates show. This year, Anthropic has released eight flagship frontier models; OpenAI has released six.'

items.slide_topic: Secondary recap of the chart (low reliability)
items.headline: AI models from OpenAI and Anthropic are now shipping every ~11 days, not months. Here's what you need to know.
items.dek: A post from @jfonsecarivera early on Sep 30, 2026 went viral for pointing out that a new frontier model from OpenAI or Anthropic used to land roughly every 10 weeks. Now the average gap between releases from the two labs is down to about 11 days.
items.outlet: X (Twitter) - AGTP (@AGTPinsights, a tech podcast account)
items.author: AGTP
items.caption: Long-form X post + infographic recapping the chart; 2,739 views at fetch.
items.notes: Do NOT cite its numbers as the chart's data: its yearly counts (2023: 4, 2024: 15, 2025: 42, 2026 YTD: 39) come from unbenchmark.com, a different dataset (see datasets). It says the post had '94,000 views, 2.8K likes, 323 quote tweets within hours' (a snapshot taken early Sep 30; current figures are 344,783 / 7,352 / 146 quotes). It also says the unbenchmark data was 'shared in the replies'; I found it only as a separate standalone post by @gitghxst (see facts).

Anthropic/OpenAI figures are as stated in the post; the page's chart shows all labs.

facts.claim: "you're not crazy / between anthropic and openai, a new model used to come out every ~10 weeks / now it's every ~11 days" - josh :) (@jfonsecarivera)

The chart's rolling-median line starts at 70 days (= the post's '~10 weeks') in early 2024 and ends at 11 days, labelled 'median gap now'; the y-axis is 'Days since the previous release (either lab)'; the grey band is 'Shaded: middle 50% of gaps'.
facts.source: Chart image attached to the post

facts.claim: The post reached 344,783 views, 7,352 likes, 491 reposts, 146 quote-posts, 165 replies, 916 bookmarks by 2026-10-05 (posted Tue Sep 29 2026 18:31 UTC).

Author: display name 'josh :)', handle @jfonsecarivera (formerly @joshycodes - old status URLs under /joshycodes/ resolve to this account), X bio 'safety fellow @AnthropicAI • I code silly things for 26k people on YouTube. Prev: @UChicago', Berkeley CA, ~2,454 followers, verified. An Anthropic Fellow per his own bio - do not describe him as an Anthropic employee/researcher.

Real name: Joshua Fonseca Rivera ('Josh Fonseca Rivera' in The Neuron). jfr.dev (personal site, 'Anthropic Fellow trying to figure out what's going on in language models') and github.com/jfonsecarivera ('Joshua Fonseca Rivera', Berkeley, links to YouTube @joshycodes) both state it, and he is first author of arXiv:2511.21399 'Steering Awareness: Detecting Activation Steering from Within'.

The Neuron's daily digest (Grant Harvey, Sep 30 2026) lists it under 'Honorable Mentions': 'Josh Fonseca Rivera charted a striking acceleration in frontier releases, arguing in a same-day post that the OpenAI and Anthropic model cadence has compressed from roughly every 10 weeks to roughly every 11 days.'

Counterpoint (Fast Company, Sep 23 2026): releases are accelerating, 'but many of the new releases are models that repackage (and often reprice) the capabilities of earlier flagship models'; 'the time between genuinely new flagship frontier models hasn't changed much during 2026'; Anthropic released eight flagship models and OpenAI six this year.
facts.source: Fast Company (Mark Sullivan) via Yahoo Finance

facts.claim: The chart plots about 35 releases (19 Anthropic squares, 16 OpenAI triangles) between 2024-03-04 and 2026-09-28, so it counts headline/flagship-type launches rather than every model (unbenchmark.com counts 15 + 42 + 39 = 96 combined releases over 2024-2026 YTD, OpenRouter's market-wide count is a launch day every 1.7 days). The author has not said what qualifies.
facts.source: Counted by me from the chart image; unbenchmark post; OpenRouter infographic

facts.claim: Same-day launches ARE in the chart as ~0-day gaps (green triangles on the 0 line, e.g. around 2026-02-04 and 2026-09-21), so the 11-day median is not inflated by dropping them.

Timing: the post came 17 days after Dario Amodei's 'We Must Pace the Frontier' essay (Sept 12, 2026) and a week after Claude Opus 5.5 / GPT-6 Sol / GPT-6 Luna launched on Sept 22; many reactions framed it as 'so much for slowing down' (e.g. @full_kelly_ 'so much for slowing down AI development', 15 likes).
